newsitem.title: USA: British nanny accused of murder denied bail.
newsitem.headline: British nanny accused of murder denied bail.

text.p: A 19-year-old British au pair accused of murdering a nine-month-old boy left in her charge was denied bail at a hearing on Monday.

Massachusetts Superior Court Judge Hiller Sobel denied bail for Louise Woodward of Chester, England, who has been held since early February on charges she killed Matthew Eappen by severely shaking the infant and then striking his head against a hard surface.
"The application is denied without prejudice," Sobel said. Prosecutors opposed any bail for Woodward, arguing she would present a risk of flight.

Woodward's lawyer, Andrew Good, failed to convince the judge, through letters of support from the teen-ager's doctor, vicar and teachers and the offer of her parent's $228,200 (140,000 sterling) home that she would not flee. Good also offered that Woodward be placed under house arrest at the home of a local lawyer with ties to the British consulate and be monitored by an electronic bracelet.
Woodward, who came to the United States in June, was arrested Feb. 6, one day after Eappen died at Children's Hospital in Boston suffering from head injuries.
She has pleaded not guilty to the charges.
Woodward had been living with the Eappen family since November working as an au pair.
